name: Demo K: Type/Family Change Redline Device
description: Exercise a type/family-change redline operation against a disposable or low-risk device target: dry-run a type change, apply it, prove readback, capture post-change evidence, then revert for repeat-safe live runs.
setup_instructions: Open a disposable Revit model or a model that can be closed without saving.
Provide an element id and compatible target type id or exact type name in the same category.
Use a low-risk target such as a fixture/device in a copied sample model so the workflow can revert after verification.
success_criteria: /revit/change-element-type dry-run returns old and new type evidence for every requested element.
/revit/change-element-type apply returns changed element ids covering every requested element.
A post-apply readback proves the element now has the requested target type id.
A post-change visual capture is produced before reverting.
The workflow reverts the element to its original type and readback proves restoration.
A type-change summary artifact is written.
failure_criteria: The dry-run cannot resolve the requested target type.
The apply response omits any requested element id.
Readback does not prove the requested target type after apply.
The revert dry-run/apply/readback omits any requested element id or fails to restore the original type.
grader_notes: This is the first type/family-change redline benchmark. It is intentionally revert-first for repeated live testing.
For real MEP cases, adapt the same evidence contract to rectangular-to-round duct, balancing damper family/type swaps, and fixture/device type swaps.
